title: MIDI export warns about flips a rack cannot play and refuses the wrong track
description:
As a beatmaker, I want to be told what the rack and MIDI cannot reproduce, and why a track cannot be exported, so that I know where the rack will sound different from Apricity.

```gherkin
Feature: MIDI export reports what cannot travel and every mistake
  Background:
    Given a sample "brk.wav" of 2 bars in 4/4 at 120 BPM, analyzed
    And the score "flip.apr" with "clip brk = brk.wav", "kit b = slice brk by beats 1" and "track b steps \"1 2 3 4\"" on line 6

  Scenario Outline: Flips a rack cannot play are warned about, with the line
    Given the track line adds "<flip>"
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps b"
    Then the export succeeds
    And it warns "flip.apr:6: <what> is not in the preset or the MIDI; the rack plays the pads without it"

    Examples:
      | flip           | what                       |
      | reverse        | reverse                    |
      | filter lp 800  | the filter                 |
      | half           | the speed change           |
      | transpose follow | following the chords     |

  Scenario: A track that plays another kit is refused
    Given the score also has "kit c = slice brk into 4" and "track c steps \"1 2\""
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps c"
    Then the export fails with "flip.apr: track `c` plays kit `c`, not `b`"
    And no file is written

  Scenario: An unknown track suggests the nearest one
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps bb"
    Then the export fails with "no track named \"bb\"; did you mean \"b\"?"

  Scenario: A track that plays a clip, not the kit, is refused
    Given the score also has "track loop = brk"
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps loop"
    Then the export fails with "track `loop` plays the clip `brk`, not kit `b`"

  Scenario: An existing MIDI file is not overwritten without --force
    Given the file "b.mid" exists
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps b"
    Then the export fails with "b.mid exists; use --force to replace it"
    And no file is written
```
